newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: BOURSE ACTIVITY SLOW AMID SUSPENSIONS.
newsitem.headline: BOURSE ACTIVITY SLOW AMID SUSPENSIONS.

text.p: Brokers said trading was especially slow Tuesday morning on Lithuania's struggling stock exchange because shareholder meetings and other business had suspended trade in several big stocks.

"It's very quiet because some companies are suspended -- Lithuanian Energy, Vilniaus Bank, Sanitas, Lithuanian Savings Bank -- because of shareholders meetings or other reasons," said Arvydas Jacikevichius, a broker with Suprema.
"The market is not very interesting today because so many copmanies were not quoted," said Grazina Bachiuliene, a broker with Vilfima. "I think turnover will be down."
"The situation for today is not very optimistic," Bachiuliene added.
Of the shares that were active, Lithuanian Gas was steady at 1.80 litas. Lithuanian Gas and Lithuanian Energy together often indicate the market's direction.

Brokers said the reorganisation of Lithuanian Energy, which is expected to separate the loss-making heating business from the more profitable electricity part, would help the company's shares when it resumes trade.
"We think it will be better for private shareholders because electricity is profitable but there were lots of losses in heating," Bachiuliene said.
The government said earlier that heating would be passed on to the municipalities.
In other trading, Dirbtinis Plaushas slid to 0.71 litas from 0.78 litas and Ragutis dipped to 18.00 litas from 18.40 litas.
Brokers expect beer brewer Ragutis to gain in the short-term as summer sets in and beer consumption rises.
